sentences.en: We get support from UC Davis, a globally ranked university working to solve the world's most pressing problems in food, energy, health, education, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 我们的赞助来自加州大学戴维斯分校，这是一所全球知名的大学，致力于解决世界在食品、能源、健康、教育和环境领域最紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: UC Davis researchers collaborate and innovate in California and around the globe to find transformational solutions.
sentences.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员在加利福尼亚州乃至全球展开合作与创新，以寻求变革性的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's all part of the university's mission to promote quality of life for all living things.
sentences.zh: 这完全符合该大学促进所有生物生活质量的使命。

sentences.en: Find out more at 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu.
sentences.zh: 访问 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu 了解更多信息。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: If you type the word courthouse into a Google image search, you get hundreds of results that look really similar to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果你在谷歌图片搜索中输入“法院”一词，你会得到几百个看起来与美国最高法院大楼非常相似的结果。

sentences.en: Supreme Court building.
sentences.zh: 最高法院大楼。

sentences.en: Big steps, a granite Corinthian colonnade topped by a grand pediment.
sentences.zh: 宽大的台阶，花岗岩的科林斯柱廊，顶部是一个宏伟的山花。

sentences.en: If the architecture could talk, it would say respect me.
sentences.zh: 如果建筑会说话，它会说：尊重我。

sentences.en: Serious S happens here.
sentences.zh: 严肃的大事就在这里发生。

sentences.en: That's Brett Myers.
sentences.zh: 那是布雷特·迈尔斯。

sentences.en: He's reporting this week's show.
sentences.zh: 他在报道本周的节目。

sentences.en: He went to the New York County Family Court in Lower Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 他去了曼哈顿下城的纽约县家事法院。

sentences.en: It's a building that looks nothing like the classic Roman and Greek-inspired architecture that most of us associate with courthouses.
sentences.zh: 这座建筑看起来一点也不像我们大多数人与法院联系在一起的经典罗马和希腊风格建筑。

sentences.en: There's little to equate family with the building beyond dysfunction.
sentences.zh: 除了失调，这座建筑几乎没有什么能让人将它与家庭联系起来。

sentences.en: If the family court could have talked before its 2006 renovation, it would have said, all who enter are doomed.
sentences.zh: 如果这家家事法院在 2006 年翻新之前会说话，它会说：凡进入此地的人都注定绝望。

sentences.en: Built in 1975, this polished black Cubist Hulk is about as welcoming as the Death Star.
sentences.zh: 这座建于 1975 年的光面黑色立体主义庞然大物，其热情好客的程度堪比死星。

sentences.en: That's Eugene Patron reading from an article he wrote about his time as a paralegal in the building.
sentences.zh: 那是尤金·帕特龙在朗读他写的一篇文章，内容关于他在这座建筑里担任律师助理的经历。

sentences.en: He sums up the most common argument about the original design.
sentences.zh: 他总结了关于最初设计的最常见的争议。

sentences.en: The New York County Family Court at 60 Lafayette Street is infamous in architecture circles as an example of form giving not a damn about function.
sentences.zh: 位于拉斐特街 60 号的纽约县家事法院在建筑界臭名昭著，它是“形式完全不顾功能”的反面典型。

sentences.en: And that's an easy argument to make.
sentences.zh: 这个论点很容易站得住脚。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: It filled me with rage the first time I saw this building back in the late 90s.
sentences.zh: 上世纪 90 年代末我第一次看到这座建筑时，它让我充满了愤怒。

sentences.en: The design just seemed so wrong for a family courthouse.
sentences.zh: 这个设计对一个家事法院来说实在太不合适了。

sentences.en: It was like hiring Dick Cheney to be the nanny for your kids.
sentences.zh: 就像雇迪克·切尼来当你的孩子的保姆一样。

sentences.en: It was brutaliSt. Think repetitive angles and thick, heavy forms and lots and lots of concrete.
sentences.zh: 它是粗野主义风格。想想重复的棱角、厚重笨拙的造型，以及许许多多的混凝土。

sentences.en: It's a pretty polarizing style, which I actually kind of like.
sentences.zh: 这是一种毁誉参半的风格，而我其实还挺喜欢的。

sentences.en: And before the 2006 remodel, it was possible to appreciate this building, but from afar.
sentences.zh: 在 2006 年改建之前，人们还可以欣赏这座建筑，但只能远观。

sentences.en: Up close was a different story.
sentences.zh: 近看又是另一回事了。

sentences.en: The shiny black granite panels that covered the whole thing were falling off and threatening to kill people on the ground.
sentences.zh: 覆盖整栋建筑的光亮黑色花岗岩面板不断脱落，威胁着地面行人的安全。

sentences.en: It was a looming and menacing building.
sentences.zh: 这是一座阴森逼人、充满威胁感的建筑。

sentences.en: Even the entrance was scary.
sentences.zh: 甚至连入口都很吓人。

sentences.en: There were these huge pylons offset at 45-degree angles so that when you entered the building, you couldn't actually see what it was you were walking into.
sentences.zh: 有这些巨大的、以 45 度角错开的桥墩，当你进入大楼时，你其实根本看不到你走进去的是什么地方。

sentences.en: It was like stepping into a black hole.
sentences.zh: 就像步入一个黑洞。

sentences.en: Definitely very bleak and very, oh my God, what is this, a black building?
sentences.zh: 绝对非常凄凉，非常“天哪，这是什么，一栋黑色的建筑？”

sentences.en: You know, is this a courthouse?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这真的是法院吗？

sentences.en: Miriam Hernandez works there as an interpreter translator.
sentences.zh: 米里亚姆·埃尔南德斯在那里担任口笔译员。

sentences.en: It didn't really have the feeling of humanity or humane, you know, it didn't really have that.
sentences.zh: 它真的没有什么人情味或人道的感觉，你知道，真的没有那种东西。

sentences.en: What kind of stuff happens inside?
sentences.zh: 里面会发生些什么样的事情？

sentences.en: Oh my God, the question should be what doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 天哪，问题应该是里面有什么事不会发生。

sentences.en: What doesn't happen?
sentences.zh: 什么事不会发生？

sentences.en: I mean, it's like you could write maybe a forever book about what takes place inside, you know?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你甚至可以写一本关于里面发生的事情的永恒之书，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And that forever book wouldn't be a light read.
sentences.zh: 而那本永恒之书绝不会是一本轻松的读物。

sentences.en: It would have chapters about custody battles and divorces and abuse, children going into family court and their fates being decided behind those doors.
sentences.zh: 它会有关于抚养权争夺、离婚和虐待的章节，孩子们走进家事法院，他们的命运就在那些门后被决定。

sentences.en: If anything, you would hope that the architecture would inspire trust, not fear, and maybe even convey a little bit of warmth.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，你都会希望建筑能够激发信任而不是恐惧，甚至也许能传达一点温暖。

sentences.en: But instead, court employees refer to it as the Darth Vader building.
sentences.zh: 但相反，法院的工作人员称它为“达斯·维达大楼”。

sentences.en: Your mother and I are getting a divorce.
sentences.zh: 你母亲和我打算离婚。

sentences.en: Pardon me, Lord.
sentences.zh: 劳驾，阁下。

sentences.en: The question is, was the form of the New York County Family Courthouse completely antithetical to its function?
sentences.zh: 问题是，纽约县家事法院的形式是否完全违背了它的功能？

sentences.en: I met a guy who's got a really interesting theory about this.
sentences.zh: 我遇到一个人，他对这个问题有一个非常有趣的理论。

sentences.en: This guy goes by the name Lofter One.
sentences.zh: 这家伙化名“阁楼一号”。

sentences.en: My Clark Kent is a, basically I do freelance research.
sentences.zh: 我的克拉克·肯特身份是，基本上我做自由撰稿的研究工作。

sentences.en: By day, he's a writer-researcher for a real estate blog.
sentences.zh: 白天，他是某房地产博客的撰稿兼研究员。

sentences.en: But his secret identity is Lofter One.
sentences.zh: 但他的秘密身份是“阁楼一号”。

sentences.en: It's the handle he uses when contributing to Wired New York, this hugely popular website about all things New York City.
sentences.zh: 这是他在“纽约有线”上发帖时使用的网名，这是一个关于纽约市方方面面的极受欢迎的网站。

sentences.en: The community section is basically a forum for urban design geeks.
sentences.zh: 社区板块基本上是城市设计极客们的论坛。

sentences.en: And Lofter One is one of the biggest geeks on the site.
sentences.zh: 而“阁楼一号”是该网站上最大的极客之一。

sentences.en: So, how many posts have you posted since June?
sentences.zh: 那么，自六月以来你发了多少帖？

sentences.en: Way too many.
sentences.zh: 太多了。

sentences.en: Way too many for a sane person.
sentences.zh: 对一个神智正常的人来说太多了。

sentences.en: About, oh, a couple thousand.
sentences.zh: 大约，哦，好几千条吧。

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不确定。

sentences.en: No, it's like 28,000, something like that.
sentences.zh: 不，大概是 28000 条，诸如此类的数字。

sentences.en: 28,131 posts.
That's as of when?
sentences.zh: 那是截至什么时候的？

sentences.en: Because you didn't check this morning, did you?
sentences.zh: 因为你今天早上没查，对吧？

sentences.en: I've added a few.
sentences.zh: 我又添了几条。

sentences.en: You've added a few today?
sentences.zh: 你今天又添了几条？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I go on there almost every day.
sentences.zh: 我几乎每天都上去。

sentences.en: In fact, he averages almost 13 posts per day.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他平均每天发帖近 13 条。

sentences.en: And most are related to architecture and urban planning.
sentences.zh: 而且大多与建筑和城市规划有关。

sentences.en: One of his first posts was about the remodel of the building we're talking about, the family courthouse, the building we're standing in front of.
sentences.zh: 他的第一批帖子之一就是关于我们正在谈论的这座建筑的改建，即那座家事法院，也就是我们正站在其门前的这座建筑。

sentences.en: That old place, I felt like I was kneeling down and crawling through a teeny little hole in a cave.
sentences.zh: 那个老地方，我觉得自己就像是跪在地上，爬过洞穴里一个小得可怜的洞。

sentences.en: And, you know, I didn't know what the hell.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我根本不知道到底是怎么回事。

sentences.en: There was a bear, there were bats, there was something on the other side.
sentences.zh: 里面有熊，有蝙蝠，另一边有什么东西。

sentences.en: What happened inside was not going to be good.
sentences.zh: 里面发生的事情绝不会是好事。

sentences.en: They should have put, you know, abound in hope, all ye who enter here, because that's what the message was sending.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们本该挂上一块“凡进入此地者，当抛弃所有希望”，因为那就是它发出的信息。

sentences.en: And Lofter One argues that that message had a time stamp.
sentences.zh: “阁楼一号”认为，那个信息是有时代局限的。

sentences.en: That old, black, shiny Death Star of a building reflected the New York of the times, the New York back in the 70s when it was built.
sentences.zh: 那座古老、黑色、闪闪发光的死星般的建筑，反映了那个时代的纽约，反映了 70 年代建造它时的纽约。

sentences.en: Well, Watergate, financial distress, social divide, it all makes total sense.
sentences.zh: 水门事件、财政困境、社会分裂，这一切都完全说得通。

sentences.en: Total sense that this building looked the way it did.
sentences.zh: 这座建筑长成这个样子完全说得通。

sentences.en: And this argument gains even more weight when you consider a 1977 story by famed New York Times reporter Lori Johnston.
sentences.zh: 当你考虑到《纽约时报》著名记者洛里·约翰斯顿在 1977 年的一篇报道时，这个论点就更有分量了。

sentences.en: The article profiles users of the court in what is essentially a critique of the system.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章通过法院使用者的视角进行了剖析，本质上是对这个系统的批判。

sentences.en: She interviews people who spend days shuffling from one waiting room to another.
sentences.zh: 她采访了那些花上一整天时间从一个候诊室辗转到另一个候诊室的人们。

sentences.en: And their critiques of the bureaucracy go hand in hand with critiques of the architecture.
sentences.zh: 他们对官僚作风的批判与对建筑的批判如出一辙。

sentences.en: Here's a quote from the 1977 article.
sentences.zh: 以下是 1977 年那篇文章中的一段引言。

sentences.en: It seems like a maze, this place.
sentences.zh: 这个地方看起来就像个迷宫。

sentences.en: Or worse, it seems like it's run like a prison with uniforms all over.
sentences.zh: 或者更糟，它看起来就像是由满眼制服的监狱在运营。

sentences.en: Maybe it's meant to discourage you from going ahead.
sentences.zh: 也许这是为了打消你继续下去的念头。

sentences.en: It's like, oh, you want form to meet function?
sentences.zh: 这就好比，哦，你想让形式服从功能？

sentences.en: This is how this court functions.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个法院运作的方式。

sentences.en: This is what this court does.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个法院所做的事。

sentences.en: It sucks people in and spits them out, and there's no feeling.
sentences.zh: 它把人们吸进去再吐出来，毫无温度可言。

sentences.en: It doesn't solve the probleMs.
sentences.zh: 它根本没有解决问题。

sentences.en: Now, of course, the courthouse has been remodeled, and it's warmer and friendlier, and it reflects a city that's friendlier and more functional.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在这座法院已经重新装修过了，它变得更温暖、更友善，也反映了一个更加友善、功能更完善的城市。

sentences.en: The black facade is all gone.
sentences.zh: 黑色的外墙全都不见了。

sentences.en: It's kind of a light gray now.
sentences.zh: 现在它有点像浅灰色。

sentences.en: And the entrance is all opened up.
sentences.zh: 而且入口完全敞开了。

sentences.en: It even has kind of an awning.
sentences.zh: 它甚至还有一个类似雨棚的东西。

sentences.en: That doesn't look imposing or unfriendly at all.
sentences.zh: 看起来一点也不威严或冷漠。

sentences.en: And there's no more threat that those black granite panels are going to fall off the side of the building and kill people.
sentences.zh: 而且再也没有那些黑色花岗岩面板从大楼侧面掉下来砸死人的威胁了。

sentences.en: And oh, yeah, it's also kind of boring.
sentences.zh: 哦，对了，它也变得有点无聊。

sentences.en: The remodel is definitely a little boring, and it's not a building I want to talk to my friends about.
sentences.zh: 改建后的建筑确实有点无聊，它不是那种我想跟朋友聊起的建筑。

sentences.en: But that original building angered me, and it was something I talked to my friends about.
sentences.zh: 但原本那座建筑激怒了我，那是我会跟朋友谈论的话题。

sentences.en: It was dark and interesting.
sentences.zh: 它黑暗而有趣。

sentences.en: And now Brett kind of misses the old building.
sentences.zh: 现在布雷特有点怀念老建筑了。

sentences.en: But I also know that I'm privileged, because I don't have to interact with it.
sentences.zh: 但我也知道我很特权，因为我不必与它打交道。

sentences.en: Because I don't have to work there, and I'm not a kid who has to walk into family court.
sentences.zh: 因为我不用在那里工作，我也不是必须走进家事法院的孩子。

sentences.en: For them, this milky, bland remodel is a definite improvement.
sentences.zh: 对他们而言，这种乳白色、平庸的改建绝对是一个改善。

sentences.en: And probably a sacrifice worth making.
sentences.zh: 而且可能也是一个值得付出的代价。

sentences.en: Come on, it's for kids, man.
sentences.zh: 拜托，这是为了孩子们，老兄。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Brett Myers and me, Roman Mars, with support from Lunar, making a difference with creativity.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由布雷特·迈尔斯和我罗曼·马尔斯制作，并得到了用创意创造改变的 Lunar 的支持。

sentences.en: It's a project of KALW Local Public Radio 91.7 in San Francisco, the American Institute of Architects in San Francisco, and the Center for Architecture and Design.
sentences.zh: 这是旧金山地方公共广播电台 KALW 91.7、旧金山美国建筑师学会以及建筑与设计中心的合作项目。

sentences.en: You can find out more at the website, it's 99percentinvisible.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在其网站上了解更多信息，网址是 99percentinvisible.org。
